title: Sourdough Starter Science
blurb: Learn fermentation behind sourdough starter magic

items.front: What two things do wild yeast and bacteria need to thrive in your starter?
items.hook: Feed them, they multiply like memes.

items.front: Why does sourdough starter smell tangy?
items.back: Lactic and acetic acids from fermentation.
items.hook: That funk? It’s alive and well.

items.front: How often should you feed a new starter?
items.hook: Neglect it, and it’ll ghost you.

items.front: What’s the ideal temp for sourdough fermentation?
items.hook: Too cold? It’s napping. Too hot? Spicy.

items.front: Why does a sourdough starter bubble?
How do you know your starter is ready to bake with?

items.text: Sourdough starters can outlive their bakers—some are over 100 years old.
Your sourdough starter’s microbiome is as unique as your fingerprint.
Ancient Egyptians used sourdough to build pyramids—it was their daily bread.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT required for a sourdough starter?
quiz.explain: Sourdough starters only need flour and water to capture wild yeast and bacteria.

quiz.q: What acids give sourdough its signature tang?
quiz.explain: Lactic and acetic acids are byproducts of fermentation in sourdough starters.

quiz.q: If your starter smells like nail polish remover, what’s wrong?
quiz.explain: A sharp, acetone-like smell means your starter is hungry and needs feeding.

quiz.q: What happens if your starter is too cold?
quiz.explain: Cold temperatures slow down fermentation, making your starter sluggish.

quiz.q: What gas makes a sourdough starter rise?
quiz.explain: Yeast metabolizes sugar and releases CO2, creating bubbles in the starter.

quiz.q: What’s a sign your starter is NOT ready to use?
quiz.explain: A starter that hasn’t doubled in size isn’t strong enough for baking yet.

quiz.q: How long can a sourdough starter last?
quiz.explain: With regular feeding and care, sourdough starters can live for decades or even centuries.

quiz.q: What makes every sourdough starter unique?
options: The local wild yeast and bacteria
quiz.explain: The wild yeast and bacteria in your environment give your starter its one-of-a-kind flavor and activity.

quiz.q: What did ancient Egyptians use sourdough for?
quiz.explain: Sourdough was a staple food for ancient Egyptians, including the workers who built the pyramids.
